entries.effect: the degenerate rectangle AT the point asked for, or CGRectNull when the device does not support exposure rectangles of interest - which is what the header says this method returns in that case (AVCaptureDevice.h:1429) and what the host's own class answers (measured: CGRectIsNull 1, for every point asked). The degenerate rectangle is the smallest rectangle the release's own unit can express: its point of interest is a CGPoint, with no extent, so a rectangle of zero size at that point names exactly it

entries.reason: neither -exposureRectOfInterest nor its setter is a selector of any release this port's bands are measured against, and the release's own substrate for it - -exposurePointOfInterest, -setExposurePointOfInterest:, -isExposurePointOfInterestSupported - is there from 6.0
entries.effect: the rectangle the caller set, kept per device; the degenerate rectangle at the release's own current exposure point of interest when none was set; and CGRectNull when the device does not support exposure rectangles of interest, which is what the host's own class answers for both rectangles (measured: inf inf 0 0, CGRectNull). The header's own effect is implemented through the release: setting it updates -exposurePointOfInterest to the centre of the rectangle (AVCaptureDevice.h:1415), and setting -exposurePointOfInterest later resets the rectangle to the default one for the new point - which a category sees by reconciling the stored rectangle's centre against the release's own point

entries.effect: whatever the release says its exposure point of interest supports, which is the derivation the header's own effect asks for: "Setting exposureRectOfInterest updates the device's exposurePointOfInterest to the center of your provided rectangle of interest" (:1415), so a device that cannot be pointed at cannot be given a rectangle either. Measured on the host, whose camera does not support either: 0 for both, the port's stand-in answers 1 where the release's substrate says the point is supported and the harness asks both branches

entries.reason: the property is 26.0's (AVCaptureDevice.h:1411) and no release this port's bands are measured against carries the selector
entries.effect: { 0, 0 }, and the reason is the geometry rather than a constant that happens to pass: the header says "The size returned is in normalized coordinates, and depends on the current AVCaptureDevice/activeFormat. If exposureRectOfInterestSupported returns false, this property returns { 0, 0 }" (:1410), and Apple's number is the smallest area the sensor's exposure metering can weigh, which it measures in the active format's sensor pixels and normalizes. The release has no such quantity anywhere - its camera device carries a point of interest and a format description and no metering area - so the smallest rectangle that still denotes a point is the degenerate one, which is the same { 0, 0 } the header documents for an unsupported device. Measured on the host: { 0, 0 }, both sides. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: the setter's size check can refuse a rectangle with a negative extent and nothing else
entries.source: the header of the SDK 26.2 (AVCaptureDevice.h:1407-1411), transcribed into CharonAVCaptureDeviceRectsOfInterest26.h
